text: Deputy PM urged Hải Phòng City to accelerate growth

HÀ NỘI - Deputy Prime Minister Nguyễn Văn Thắng has urged the northern port city of Hải Phòng to strive for the highest possible economic growth in 2026, saying its strong performance will make a significant contribution to the country's ambition of achieving double-digit growth.

At a meeting with municipal authorities on November 18, Thắng said Hải Phòng City, one of Việt Nam's major industrial and logistics hubs, should aim higher than its own growth target and further strengthen its role as a national growth driver.
The Government expects major economic centres, including Hà Nội, HCM City, Hải Phòng and Quảng Ninh, to make greater efforts to support the country's growth ambitions, he said.

Hải Phòng City's gross regional domestic product (GRDP) grew by an estimated 12.08 per cent in the first nine months of 2026, ranking third among 34 provinces and cities and placing it among the three localities that recorded growth of at least 12 per cent.
The city's economy was valued at approximately VNĐ612 trillion (US$23.2 billion), accounting for 5.8 per cent of national economic output, according to a report by the municipal People's Committee.
State budget revenue reached VNĐ181 trillion in the first 10 months, equivalent to 92.9 per cent of the annual target and up 10.12 per cent year-on-year.
Foreign direct investment (FDI) attraction totalled $3.8 billion, up 69 per cent from a year earlier and equivalent to 96.4 per cent of the annual target.
Public investment disbursement stood at VNĐ33.88 trillion as of October 31, reaching 91.76 per cent of the plan assigned by the Prime Minister.
Industrial production remained a key growth driver, with the industrial production index (IIP) rising 15.12 per cent in the first 10 months, compared with national growth of 12.4 per cent.
Manufacturing and processing output increased 14.99 per cent.
Retail sales of goods and service revenue rose 16.17 per cent, outpacing the national increase of 13.5 per cent.
Exports reached an estimated $50.1 billion, up 10.9 per cent year-on-year, while imports climbed 18.8 per cent to $40.1 billion, resulting in a trade surplus of $10 billion.
Cargo throughput at the city's seaports reached approximately 182.4 million tonnes, up 12.11 per cent, while revenue from transportation, warehousing and related services increased 20.8 per cent.

Deputy PM Thắng also highlighted Hải Phòng City's contribution to national energy security, noting that its existing thermal power plants have a combined capacity of 3,440 MW and help supply electricity to the national grid.

The Deputy Prime Minister called on the city to accelerate growth in the remaining months of the year, with a focus on speeding up public investment disbursement to fulfil 100 per cent of its annual plan.
He also urged local authorities to maintain stable supplies of essential goods and fuel ahead of year-end and the upcoming Tết (Lunar New Year) holiday to help contain inflationary pressures.

In attracting investment, Hải Phòng City should prioritise high-tech manufacturing and supporting-industry projects, with a focus on semiconductors, electronics, precision engineering, electric vehicles, clean energy, maritime industries and logistics.
Deputy PM Thắng stressed that rapid industrial expansion must go hand in hand with efficient land and energy use, environmental protection and sustainable development.

He also called for a comprehensive development strategy and coordination mechanism covering the city's economic zones, industrial parks and free trade zones to ensure clear functional roles and complementary investment priorities, while avoiding overlapping projects and inefficient resource allocation.
The city should further strengthen exports by making better use of free trade agreements, exploring new markets and expanding cross-border e-commerce and direct distribution channels.
Efforts should also be stepped up to help businesses meet rules of origin, technical standards and traceability requirements, while mitigating trade defence risks and preventing origin fraud.

On infrastructure, Deputy PM Thắng said Hải Phòng City should make better use of its seaport system and connect economic zones, industrial parks and free trade zones to transform itself from a cargo transit point into a regional centre for supply-chain value creation and distribution.

The Deputy Prime Minister said the Government and central ministries would continue working with Hải Phòng to address difficulties involving land, planning, investment mechanisms, port infrastructure and energy projects.
Việt Nam is stepping up efforts to achieve 10 per cent economic growth in 2026.
To reach that annual target, national GDP growth in the fourth quarter will need to reach approximately 12.5 per cent.
Chairman of the municipal People's Committee Đỗ Thành Trung said the city would strive to fulfil its 2026 targets to lay a solid foundation for a new phase of development.

During a visit to the centralised customs clearance area at Customs Sub-Department Region III on the same day, Deputy PM Thắng called for smooth operations and an early review and further refinement of one-stop clearance procedures for possible nationwide expansion.

The Deputy Prime Minister also tasked the Ministry of Finance and relevant ministries and agencies with cutting unnecessary specialised inspection procedures while maintaining effective oversight and creating the most favourable conditions for importers and exporters. - VNS
